2. The appeal is filed to set aside the judgment dated 21.06.2021, passed by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere, in A.P.No.17/2020 as far as the direction for the payment of solatium and the statutory interest to respondents 1 to 5 is concerned, and consequently to restore the Arbitral Award dated 21st August 2017, passed by the sixth respondent.

sentences.text: 3. The Central Government, for the construction of four laning from Kms.378.200 to Kms.418.500 (Hospet to Chitradurga Section) issued a final notification under Section 3D (1) and (2) of the National Highways Act.

The same was published in the official gazette, declaring that amongst other lands, the lands in Survey No.19/P11 to an extent of 1,111 NC: 2026:KHC:6275 HC-KAR square meters situated at the said village rest absolutely with the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

The seventh respondent was appointed as the competent authority under Section 3(a) of the National Highways Act, determined the value at Rs.2,00,000/- per acre, equivalent to Rs.49.50/- per square meter vide award dated 26.03.2013.
Being dissatisfied with the market value determined by respondent No.7, Sri.Nanjappa, the owner of the acquired lands, approached respondent No.6 seeking enhancement of compensation.

The sixth respondent, with a common arbitral award dated 21.08.2017, rejected the claims of the land owners, including that of Sri.Nanjappa, thereby confirming the market value determined by the seventh respondent.

The respondents 1 to 5, the legal representatives of Late Sri.Nanjappa, aggrieved by the Arbitral Award, approached the Principal District and Session Judge at Davangere by filing a suit under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 seeking setting aside the Arbitral Award and enhancement of the compensation., which later came to be registered as A.P.No.17/2020 and after transfer to and re- transfer from Commercial Court to the Principal District and NC:
2026:KHC:6275 HC-KAR Sessions Judge, Davanagare.

entities.text: Principal District and Session Judge at Davangere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellant, through its counsel,
contested the matter by way of filing a written statement, contended that there was no scope for modification of the arbitral award, and the relief sought in the petition was outside the scope of Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
The appellant also brought to the notice of the District Court that, as on the date of the hearing of the main arguments, the application seeking modification of the order dated 19.09.2019 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court was still pending before the Supreme Court.
The District Court after dismissing the suit, passed further orders awarding solatium and statutory interest on the market value determined by the respondent No.7.
Under these circumstances, the appellant has filed the appeal on several grounds as setout in the Memorandum of appeal.

sentences.text: In the present case, the lands were acquired for a public purpose and compensation was duly awarded by the SLAO; the arbitrator rightly rejected the petition on 21.08.2017.
As the suit was dismissed, the Trial Court acted without jurisdiction in awarding solatium and interest.

It is a well-settled principle of law that under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
1996, the Court's jurisdiction is confined to either upholding or setting aside an NC:
2026:KHC:6275 HC-KAR arbitral award; it does not possess the power to modify the award's substantive findings.
Moreover, the claimants did not pray for the grant of solatium and statutory interest; hence, the award of solatium and interest is untenable.
In the absence of a plea for the grant of solatium and statutory interest, the award of the same was untenable.
Needless to observe upon dismissal of the suit, the Court became functus officio regarding the subject matter, rendering the award of solatium and interest is null and void.
Counsel for the respective parties placed reliance on the decisions referred to supra.
But I do not think that the law is in doubt.
Each decisions turns on its own facts.
The present case is also tested in the light of the aforesaid decisions.

8. For the foregoing reasons, the appeal deserves to be allowed and the judgment dated 21.06.2021,
passed by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere, in A.P.No.17/2020 as far as the direction for the payment of solatium and the statutory interest to respondents 1 to 5 is set aside,
and the Arbitral Award dated 21st August 2017, passed by the sixth respondent, is restored.
NC: 2026:KHC:6275 HC-KAR 9.

sentences.text: Resultantly, the appeal is allowed.
